## Target context
- Repo: DontPanic
- Env: dev
- Project: (none)
- Command: 2 (see structured target_context.commands_run)

[F011] I implemented the F011 core engine as a new pure module `scripts/dontpanic_orchestrate/skill_invocation.py` with two layers: (1) a Pydantic-validated `invocation:` SKILL.md frontmatter schema (`mode` enum over all six values, lifecycle stages, required inputs, risk flags, evidence target, optional command template) whose `parse_invocation` is a strict no-op for skills lacking the block (AC1), and (2) a pure `evaluate(SkillInvocationContext) → list[SkillAction]` evaluator that emits typed records across the five recommendation values with no I/O, network, or execution (AC2). Deterministic risk precedence (AC6) is implemented in fixed order — `never_suggest` opt-out → suppressed/`not_applicable` (AC12), `never_auto` → suggest, any of the six risk flags or missing inputs blocks auto-run regardless of declared mode, and an auto mode declared alongside an auto-blocking flag (or a malformed block) yields a diagnostic `approval_required` rather than silently trusting the unsafe declaration; metadata-less applicable skills default to `suggest` and are never auto-run (AC3). The auto-run allowlist stays an *injected* `is_command_allowlisted` predicate owned by F015 — the engine only classifies auto_run-eligible vs suggest based on its result. I added SKILL.md fixtures for all 13 representative skills (AC13) and a 36-test suite covering every recommendation class, the no-auto fallback, the never_suggest opt-out, contradictory-metadata precedence (parametrized over all risk flags), missi
